scenario: AITA for not making my 7 year old brother go to sleep? | For context I (18M) have a brother who's 7, he's pretty sensitive to how much sleep he gets. If he gets less sleep than normal he will be all out of sorts the next day. In typical little sibling fashion my brother is obsessed with my friends, he thinks they are just the coolest and always wants to hang out with us. My friends who don't have little siblings think he's so cute and always hype him up and stuff. Last night my mom left me in charge because she wasn't going to be home until like 1am, and she said it was fine if I had my one friend over because she trusts him. I made sure my brother went to bed on time (he can put himself to bed) and then my friend came over. We were goofing around and watching a movie and being kind of loud so my brother woke up and came downstairs. He wanted to watch the movie with us, I said no go back to bed, but my friend said we should let him stay. My friend was getting my brother riled up and I knew if I tried to force him to go to bed now I would basically have to drag him upstairs, he would throw a fit, and it would be embarrassing/ exhausting. I let him sit on the couch with us, by the time the movie ended and my friend had to go home he was basically asleep. I carried him upstairs (it was like midnight) and put him in bed. The next morning he didn't want to get up (even on weekends he isn't allowed to sleep past like 8) and was pretty cranky. My mom said she knows I let him stay up late and got mad at me. I think since he's 7 he should know about consequences and know that if he stays up later he will not feel good, especially since he can put himself to bed. I also told her 2 hours of missed sleep for a kid his age was not a big deal. AITA for not forcing him to go to bed?

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether it's right or wrong for me not to make my 7-year-old brother go to sleep when he stayed up late watching a movie with my friend. Let me break this down step by step. First, I know that my brother is pretty sensitive to how much sleep he gets. If he doesn't get enough sleep, he gets all out of sorts the next day. That makes sense because kids his age need a lot of sleep to grow and function properly. So, in an ideal situation, I should make sure he goes to bed on time. But last night, my mom left me in charge and trusted me to handle things. She even said it was fine if I had my one friend over. I made sure my brother went to bed on time, and he can put himself to bed, which is good. Then my friend came over, and we were goofing around, watching a movie, and being kind of loud. My brother woke up and came downstairs, wanting to watch the movie with us. I said, "No, go back to bed," but my friend said we should let him stay. My friend was getting my brother riled up, and I knew if I tried to force him to go to bed now, I would basically have to drag him upstairs, he would throw a fit, and it would be embarrassing and exhausting. So, I let him sit on the couch with us. By the time the movie ended and my friend had to go home, he was basically asleep. I carried him upstairs and put him in bed. It was like midnight. The next morning, he didn't want to get up, even though on weekends he isn't allowed to sleep past like 8. He was pretty cranky. My mom said she knows I let him stay up late and got mad at me. I think since he's 7, he should know about consequences and know that if he stays up later, he won't feel good, especially since he can put himself to bed. I also told her that two hours of missed sleep for a kid his age wasn't a big deal. So, the question is: Is it right or wrong for me not to force him to go to bed? I need to figure out whether my decision was correct or not. First, I need to consider the importance of sleep for a 7-year-old. According to experts, children that age typically need about 10-12 hours of sleep per night. Missing two hours might not seem like a big deal, but it can still affect their mood, behavior, and ability to function the next day. On the other hand, I was in a situation where I was trying to manage both my brother and my friend. I didn't want to cause a scene or exhaust myself by dragging him upstairs. Plus, my friend was hyping him up, making it harder for him to calm down and go to bed. I also need to think about the bigger picture. My mom trusted me to handle things, and I did make sure he went to bed on time initially. But when he woke up, I had to make a decision in the moment. Was it better to enforce the bedtime strictly, potentially causing a tantrum and stress for everyone, or to let him stay up a bit longer to avoid the conflict? Another thing to consider is teaching him about consequences. If he stays up late, he should understand that he might feel tired or cranky the next day. But at the same time, he's only 7, and it's my responsibility as his older brother to guide him, not just enforce rules strictly. I also need to think about how my mom reacted. She got mad at me for letting him stay up late. Does that mean she thinks it's wrong not to enforce bedtime strictly? Or is she just concerned about his well-being? Maybe I should have found a middle ground. Instead of letting him stay up until midnight, I could have set a compromise, like letting him watch a little more of the movie but then going to bed earlier than usual. That way, he still gets some sleep, and I avoid the conflict. Also, I need to consider the impact on myself. Being responsible for both my brother and my friend can be stressful. I need to find ways to manage these situations without getting too exhausted or causing unnecessary stress for everyone involved. In the end, I think it's a bit of both. Not enforcing bedtime strictly might not be ideal, but in the moment, it was the best decision to avoid a bigger conflict. However, it's also important to communicate with my brother about the importance of sleep and the consequences of staying up too late. Maybe next time, I can set clearer expectations upfront, so he knows what to expect, and I can handle the situation more smoothly without causing a scene.
